meta.title: lpdf Showcase — Ruling in sections
meta.subject: a ruling on every page, under layers and a background, in columns, in a markdown, with a bleed, and alone

column.text: Line 1 of the notes. The ruling's lines run across the area inside the margin, every 16pt, on each page the flow takes.
The squares run from the left edge of the page to the right one, across both columns, the gap and the rule between them, as they would without columns.
The text of the first column fills it from the top, and what is left goes on in the second column, over the same squares.

A ruling belongs to the page, not to the columns of its flow. Its lines are where they would be on a page of one column, and a column starts wherever its margin and the gap put it, on a line or between two.
The squares are 5mm, and the page is A4, 210mm wide: 42 of them fit across it exactly, so there is a line on the right edge as there is on the left one.
Down the page they don't fit exactly: 297mm is 59 squares and 2mm over, and the last row at the foot of the page is the 2mm that is left.
The text keeps to its own lines. It does not snap to the squares: a ruling is drawn under the flow and changes nothing in how the flow is laid out.
To write on the lines, set the gap between the paragraphs and their line height so that one line of text is a whole number of squares.
The column rule is drawn over the squares, as everything in the flow is, and so is the text of both columns.
A ruling in a section of columns is drawn once for the page, not once for each column.

# In a markdown
The area inside the markdown's margin is cut into eight columns and eight rows, with lines on all four edges, under the heading and this paragraph.

layout.text: The background runs into the 5mm bleed, which the press cuts off. The squares stop at the trim edge.
